overview: Whitby sits at the mouth of the River Esk, and its main surf beach is West Cliff Beach, running north-west from the West Pier towards Sandsend. Above it is the West Cliff, the Victorian side of town, with the Pavilion, a statue of Captain Cook and the whalebone arch. Across the harbour, the ruins of Whitby Abbey stand on the East Cliff at the top of the 199 Steps.

The National Park describes West Cliff as a large, shallow-gradient sandy beach with great beginner and intermediate waves, and an ideal place to learn or progress at surfing or paddleboarding. There's a beach management centre with chalet hire, showers, toilets and a café, plus deckchairs and a children's paddling pool. RNLI lifeguards patrol through the summer.

On the other side of the river, Tate Hill is a smaller, sheltered sandy beach where dogs are allowed all year. If you want a longer walk, the sands carry on from West Cliff all the way to Sandsend at low tide. Tate Hill also sits right below the old town, so it's handy if you're staying on the East Cliff side, and both beaches have the abbey as a backdrop.

text: West Cliff is a sandy beach and pier break. Surf-forecast describes it as fairly exposed with consistent surf at all stages of the tide, best on an east-north-east swell with south-westerly offshore winds. The gentle slope is what makes it so friendly for learning.

The West Pier shapes the town end of the beach, so keep well away from the harbour entrance and its boat traffic. Surf-forecast notes it's often crowded, so give lessons and swimmers room and use the lifeguarded area in season.

Whitby works best on a north or north-north-east to south-east swell between about one and six feet, with a south-westerly wind cleaning it up. Low to mid tide on the rise gives the best shape. The paddle-out is easy beside the harbour wall, and the harbour end is sheltered when it's rough. Autumn is the pick of the seasons, and the lineup is friendly rather than crowded. The usual cautions apply: rips and a few rocks, and keep clear of the harbour entrance.

cards.label: Level
cards.title: Beginners to intermediates
cards.text: A large, shallow-gradient sandy beach, per the National Park.

cards.label: Conditions
cards.title: ENE swell, SW wind
cards.text: Surf-forecast rates east-north-east swell with south-westerly winds best; works through the tide.

cards.label: Hazards
cards.title: Pier and harbour mouth
cards.text: Keep away from the West Pier and harbour entrance; expect crowds on good days.

practical.label: Lifeguards
practical.title: RNLI, 10am–6pm
practical.text: In 2026 RNLI lifeguards covered weekends and bank holidays from 2 to 17 May, then patrolled daily from 23 May to 6 September.

practical.label: Dogs
practical.title: South end banned 1 May–30 Sep
practical.text: Dogs are banned on West Beach from the West Pier to about halfway along the beach chalets from 1 May to 30 September. Tate Hill beach welcomes dogs all year but they must be on a lead there from 1 May to 30 September, and on the promenade between the Pavilion and the chalets year-round.

practical.label: Facilities
practical.title: Beach management centre
practical.text: Chalet hire, showers, toilets and a café on West Cliff Beach, plus deckchair and windbreak hire.

practical.label: Walk
practical.title: Along the sands to Sandsend
practical.text: The beach runs continuously north-west to Sandsend — check tide times before you set off.

practical.label: Getting here
practical.title: Esk Valley line
practical.text: Whitby's only regular passenger rail link is the Esk Valley line to Middlesbrough; North Yorkshire Moors Railway steam trains run from Pickering in summer.

practical.label: Parking
practical.title: Pay parking on North Promenade
practical.text: Paid parking is available on the promenade above the beach.

faqs.q: Is Whitby good for learning to surf?
faqs.a: Yes. The National Park describes West Cliff Beach as a large, gently sloping sandy beach with great beginner and intermediate waves, and there's a surf school on the beach.

faqs.q: Can I take my dog on Whitby beach?
faqs.a: Between 1 May and 30 September dogs are banned from the southern part of West Beach, from the West Pier to about halfway along the chalets. Tate Hill beach on the east side allows dogs all year, on a lead in summer.
In 2026 RNLI lifeguards covered weekends from 2 May and patrolled daily from 23 May to 6 September, 10am to 6pm.
Surf-forecast says West Cliff produces surf at all stages of the tide, though the beach is much narrower at high water.
